ASHCOMBE HARBOUR AUTHORITY — NOTICE TO MARINERS No. 14

The harbourmaster gives notice that the regulations set out below apply to every vessel moored, anchored or manoeuvring within the limits of the port from the first day of March until further notice, and that ignorance of a notice is not a defence.

Approach and fairway. Vessels approaching from the south-west shall keep the green buoy to starboard and shall not attempt to overtake a loaded dredger in the narrows. The fairway between the west pier and the inner mole is one hundred and ten metres wide at its narrowest point, and no vessel shall anchor in that stretch on any account. Masters of vessels longer than sixty metres shall take a pilot before crossing the bar. A vessel that touches the ground in the approach channel shall report the grounding to the harbour office at once, whether or not damage is apparent.

Speed. Inside the harbour walls the speed of every vessel shall not exceed four knots; in the inner basin the limit is two knots. The wash of a fast launch has twice undermined the stonework of the fish quay, and the authority will not hesitate to prosecute owners who ignore this limit. Patrol officers may board any vessel in order to measure its speed over a marked distance.

Radio. Every vessel over twenty metres shall keep a listening watch on channel twelve while under way. Calls to the harbour office shall be brief and shall state the vessel's name, position and draft. Silence on the distress channel is to be observed at all times except in the case of an emergency, and a vessel that has nothing to report shall not call merely to test its set.

Bunkering. No fuel shall be transferred between sunset and sunrise. Hoses shall be connected before the pump is started and shall be lashed at both ends. Drip trays shall be placed beneath every connection, and any spill, however small, shall be reported to the harbour office and to the coastguard before the vessel sails.

Fishing gear. Nets shall not be set within fifty metres of a navigation buoy, and gear lost overboard shall be reported with its position so that the chart can be corrected. The authority may recover abandoned gear at the owner's expense.

Tenders and dinghies. Dinghies shall be stored on the racks provided and not left on the quay or against the bollards. Outboard motors shall be drained of fuel before a dinghy is lifted out for the winter, and trailers shall not be parked where they obstruct the slipway.

Fire and safety. Every vessel carrying more than twelve passengers shall hold a current fire certificate and shall keep two serviceable extinguishers at the after end of the accommodation. Lifebuoys shall be stowed where they can be reached without opening a locker.

Mooring. Lines shall be tended in a seamanlike manner throughout the vessel's stay, and any slack line observed by the patrol shall be reported to the berthing office without delay. Vessels berthing on the west quay shall pass a spring line ashore before the engine is stopped, and shall not rely on the wind to hold them against the wall. Fenders shall be rigged on both sides during any period of more than twelve hours alongside.

Incident reports. Any collision, grounding, fire, spill or injury on board shall be reported to the harbour office by the quickest available means. Reports shall be made on the form supplied by the authority within twenty-four hours of the event.

Penalties. A master who breaks these regulations is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale, and the authority may move or detain the vessel at the owner's expense.

Charts and notices. The latest notice to mariners is posted at the harbour office and on the board beside the lifeboat station. Masters are advised to check the board before every departure.

Harbour office, West Pier, Ashcombe. Open 0800 to 1700 on weekdays, and by radio at all hours.
